text:
Jess: FYI I'm seeing steady memory growth on long-context production runs when continuous batching is enabled. 30m job goes from ~2.1GB KV -> ~3.8GB and never drops.
Kevin: which model / quant / runtime flags? can you repro locally?
Jess: repro on rdx-small (16k context), int8 qkv, runtime v0.38. Kernel selection set to auto. repro steps: run long-seq generator with steady prefix churn. paste of top logs: 
```
[2024-05-22T14:12:01Z] kv_cache_total: 2193452800 bytes
[2024-05-22T14:42:01Z] kv_cache_total: 3852345600 bytes
fragmentation_ratio: ~0.24
num_pages_evicted: 0
```
Alia: interesting - fragmentation that high + zero evictions suggests we aren't paging at slab granularity. continuous-batching merge might be creating tiny allocations that don't compact.
Rahul: can you dump per-batch KV meta? I suspect batch-merge / split is producing incompatible KV slices so reuse is low and we keep allocating new pages. Also head-of-line blocking could keep older KV entries pinned.
Jess: posted a short extractor output showing per-request kv_id and length: 
```
request 1: kv_id=A len=4096 pinned=true
request 2: kv_id=B len=4096 pinned=false
request 3: kv_id=C len=8192 pinned=true
// merge produced batch [1,2,3] then split -> 1 and 3 keep pins, 2 gets new allocation later
```
Kevin: that pattern will fragment. If merge mixes requests with different prefix-depths we can't reuse contiguous pages. We need a merge policy that groups by kv-shape and last-kv-version.
perf-bot: alert: continuous-batching memory-growth anomaly detected for endpoint /generate (p95 mem +78% over 1h).
Alia: another angle: kernel temp allocations (attention kernel) can allocate transient buffers sized to max_seq_in_batch; when we merge a short and a long request, kernel chooses a kernel variant with larger temporaries and that can push allocator into higher arenas -> fragmentation. kernel selection + batching heuristics interacting badly.
Rahul: good call. Two follow-ups: (1) add a cheap compatibility key for batches: (kv_layout_hash, max_prefix_len_bucket) and refuse to merge incompatible ones; (2) implement periodic compaction / page reclaim for KV cache that coalesces free pages when fragmentation_ratio > 0.15.
Jess: quick experiment: set --continuous-batching-merge=false and run same workload. memory plateaued at ~2.2GB (no growth). throughput dropped 6% but latency more stable.
Kevin: that's promising. We should add a toggle that allows merge only when kv_layout_hash matches, instead of global off. Also block merging if any request has pinned=true.
Alia: implementation note: we need to propagate KV-version cookie in the batch descriptor so split/merge can fast-check reuse. Also add per-page last-touch timestamp to allow LRU-style eviction for pages not referenced by current live KV slices.
Rahul: on eviction: don't evict pages blindly, prefer to page out large contiguous runs and remap pointer ranges so we avoid internal fragmentation. Might need a compacting GC for KV cache to defragment long-lived runs.
Jess: created perf-run/172 on staging with per-batch compatibility check. Preliminary: fragmentation ratio down to 0.07, mem growth eliminated, merge still gives 3% throughput win.
Kevin: nice. action items:
- Jess: open PR for batch compatibility gating + tests (unit + perf harness)
- Alia: spike compacting GC for KV pages (design doc)
- Rahul: add kernel-selection test matrix in CI to ensure we don't pick heavy-temp kernels when mixing prefix lengths
- Infra: add a regression perf test that runs 1h long-context + continuous batching.
Jess: I'll post the PR link and attach the pprof heap diff. thanks all :thumbsup:
